page: Microsoft Azure E64_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Ev5 instance family. It is equipped with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz. The processor features 105 MB of L3 cache, alongside AVX-512 and cryptography instruction set extensions. System memory totals 512.0 GB of RAM, offering a high allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance configuration includes no bundled local storage and has zero integrated GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the E64_v5 exhibits strong multi-core performance, achieving high relative results in multi-threaded workloads such as bzip3 decompression, software compilation using Clang, static web serving throughput, and multi-core CPU stress tests. Memory throughput tests demonstrate strong large-block uncached read speeds of 286.33 GB/sec and write speeds of 130.34 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing benchmarks perform within the average range, while CPU-based LLM inference throughput drops during large parameter model generation.

The hardware profile provides high memory capacity alongside substantial multi-threaded processing power, making it cost-efficient for memory-heavy enterprise software where local disk storage is managed via attached network storage. Due to its 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high memory bandwidth, the Microsoft Azure E64_v5 is suitable for in-memory databases, large-scale data analytics, enterprise relational databases, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.
